title: Nvidia reports Q3 FY27 today — Colette Kress's first earnings as interim CEO
subtitle: After Jensen Huang's November 12 resignation, CFO Colette Kress steps into the top job for the call, against a $108 billion ±2% revenue guide and a stock down roughly 20% since the last report.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Nvidia reports its fiscal 2027 third-quarter results after the U.S. market close on November 17, with the press release expected around 1:20 p.m. Pacific time and the call at 2 p.m. CFO Colette Kress, who took the interim CEO role after Jensen Huang's November 12 resignation, will host her first earnings call wearing both hats while the board's succession search continues. Nvidia's own outlook calls for revenue of $108.0 billion plus or minus 2%, a 74.0% gross margin, and roughly $9.0–9.2 billion in operating expenses, with no data-center compute revenue assumed from China. LSEG consensus among sell-side analysts is slightly higher, at about $109.2 billion on the top line and adjusted EPS of $2.47–2.49; Visible Alpha puts data-center revenue at roughly $101.8 billion.

The read-through to the AI build-out matters more than the print itself. Nvidia's results have become the single clearest proxy for hyperscaler capex intentions — the guide for next quarter effectively tells the market whether Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta, Amazon, Oracle and the growing neocloud tier are still placing orders at the rate the last six quarters implied. Blackwell remains the vast majority of revenue; Vera Rubin is in early sampling, with inventory reportedly rising to around $31.6 billion ahead of the full ramp. The stock is down roughly 20% since the last report amid the CEO transition and broader AI-infrastructure worries.

Three questions dominate the call. First, how Kress frames the leadership transition — the board has not disclosed whether Huang's departure was prompted by the reported affair allegations surfaced before his resignation, and investors want a timeline for a permanent CEO. Second, whether the China headwind narrows: Nvidia has excluded China data-center compute from guidance for several quarters, but the Trump administration's December 2025 H200 licensing shift and ongoing MOFCOM disputes keep that assumption live. Third, how quickly Rubin NVL144 shipments ramp into the first half of calendar 2027, given reported Kyber NVL144 delays into 2028 and the PCB-midplane work behind them.

A note for learners: a single earnings call is not the right unit of analysis for an infrastructure cycle this large. Watch three things across calls instead — the directional change in data-center guidance, named customer disclosures (hyperscalers versus neoclouds versus sovereigns), and gross-margin trajectory through a product transition. Those three together tell you whether demand is still outrunning supply or whether the ramp has started to normalize.
